title.value: On Weak NIZKs, One-Way Functions and Amplification
On Weak NIZKs, One-Way Functions and Amplification

abstract.value: An .(Es, E zk)-weak non-interactive zero knowledge (NIZK) argument has soundness error at most .Es and zero-knowledge error at most .E zk. We show that as long as .NP is hard in the worst case, th e existence of an .(Es, E zk)-weak NIZK proofor argument for .NP with .E zk + √ Es < 1 implies the existence of one-way functions. To obtain this result, we introduce and analyze a strong version of universal approximation that may be of independent interest. As an application, we obtain NIZK amplification theorems based on very mild worst-case complexity assumptions. Specifically, [Bitansky-Geier, CRYPTO'24] showed that .(Es, E zk)-weak NIZK proofs (with .Es and .E zk constants such that .Es + E zk < 1) can be amplified to make their errors negligible, but needed to assume the existence of one-way functions. Our results can be used to remove the additional one-way function assumption and obtain NIZK amplification theorems that are (almost) unconditional; only requiring the mild worst-case assumption that if .NP ⊆ ioP/poly, then .NP ⊆ BPP.
